headline: SECP Regulatory Sandbox Guidelines Issued
annotation: SECP issued Regulatory Sandbox Guidelines in 2019. Firms in the sectors SECP regulates could test new products under supervision, in cohorts, before full licensing. This gave capital market and non bank finance innovators a supervised path to market.
sourcePublisher: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
sourceTitle: Regulatory sandbox
label: Primary

headline: National Payment Systems Strategy (NPSS) Published
annotation: SBP launched the National Payment Systems Strategy on 1 November 2019. It set out SBP's plan for Pakistan's digital payment infrastructure, which builders can read as the background to the instant payment rail that followed. It is a strategy, not a binding rule.
sourceTitle: Digital Financial Services, with the National Payment Systems Strategy
label: Primary

headline: Raast Bulk Payments Module Launched
annotation: The first phase of Pakistan's instant payment system went live with bulk disbursements such as government salaries, pensions and social grants. For builders, this established the core clearing infrastructure that P2P and P2M modules would later plug into. Integration required connecting through SBP's participant framework.
sourceTitle: PM launches Raast, Pakistan's instant payment system (press release)
label: Primary

headline: Digital Bank Licensing Framework Issued
annotation: SBP created two licence types: Digital Retail Bank (DRB) and Digital Full Bank (DFB). A DRB needs minimum capital of PKR 1.5 billion at the pilot stage, rising to PKR 4 billion by the third year after launch. A fintech can now seek a banking licence without physical branches. The framework requires strong digital governance and data management, so any aspiring neobank needs to design for these from day one.
sourceTitle: BPRD Circular No. 01 of 2022: Licensing and Regulatory Framework for Digital Banks
label: Primary

headline: Raast P2P Instant Transfers Go Live
annotation: The second phase of Raast went live. Customers can send money instantly and free of charge to an IBAN or to a Raast ID, which at first is the customer's registered mobile number. For builders, this opened the door to embedding instant transfers into wallets, lending apps or marketplaces through participating banks.
sourceTitle: DI&SD Circular No. 1 of 2022: Raast Person to Person (P2P) Payment Service
label: Primary

headline: Revised EMI Regulations 2023 Issued
annotation: SBP revised the regulations for Electronic Money Institutions. EMIs may offer payment and bill aggregation, escrow for domestic online commerce with SBP approval, secure APIs to other firms after notifying SBP, and inward remittances to wallets with SBP permission. The regulations also cover wallets for minors, including minors who work as freelancers. If you are building a wallet or payment product, these regulations define your ceiling.
sourceTitle: PSP&OD Circular No. 03 of 2023: Regulations for Electronic Money Institutions (revised June 2023)
label: Primary

headline: Personal Data Protection Bill 2023: Final Draft
annotation: MoITT published a final draft of the Personal Data Protection Bill in May 2023. The state news agency reported in July 2023 that the federal cabinet had approved it. The draft would set up a National Commission for Personal Data Protection and would require consent, breach notification and controls on cross border transfers. The World Bank's 2026 regional assessment lists Pakistan's data protection law as a draft. It is a bill, not law. Any fintech handling personal data can still design consent management and data audit trails now.
sourceTitle: Personal Data Protection Bill, final draft, May 2023
label: Primary

headline: Regulatory Sandbox Opened to Applications All Year
annotation: SECP moved its sandbox from intake in cohorts to applications all year round, across three streams: Islamic finance, conventional finance, and businesses run by women. Startups can now apply whenever their product is ready rather than wait for the next cohort window.
sourcePublisher: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan
sourceTitle: SECP's Regulatory Sandbox shifts to 'Always Open' (press release)
label: Primary

headline: Five Digital Bank In Principle Approvals Granted
annotation: SBP gave In Principle Approval to five proposed digital retail banks: HugoBank, KT Bank Pakistan, Mashreq Bank Pakistan, Raqami Islamic Digital Bank, and Telenor Microfinance Bank (later Easypaisa Bank). The digital bank framework was moving from policy to execution, and service providers could start preparing integrations.
sourceTitle: SBP awards In Principle Approval to five proposed digital retail banks (press release)
label: Primary

headline: Raast P2M Service Launched
annotation: Merchant payments on Pakistan's instant payment rail became operational. All regulated entities had to let customers scan Raast P2M QR codes and handle merchant payment requests on their apps by 1 March 2024, free of charge to customers. For builders, any merchant facing product can now accept instant payments through a standard QR flow rather than proprietary integrations.
sourceTitle: PSP&OD Circular No. 04 of 2023: Launch of Raast Person to Merchant (P2M) Service
label: Primary

headline: First Digital Retail Bank License Granted
annotation: Easypaisa Bank Limited became Pakistan's first licensed digital retail bank, authorised for commercial operations. This is the proof point that the 2022 framework delivers licences. Competing fintechs now face a licensed digital first competitor with Telenor's distribution reach. Mashreq Bank Pakistan received a restricted licence for pilot operations on 21 February 2025.
sourceTitle: SBP awards first Digital Retail Bank licence to Easypaisa Bank Limited (press release)
label: Primary

extraSources.title: SBP awards pilot licence to Mashreq Bank Pakistan Limited to operate as Digital Retail Bank (press release)
extraSources.label: Primary

headline: Raast Participation Criteria Published
annotation: SBP opened Raast access beyond banks to fintechs, payment aggregators, and even educational institutions through four participant categories (in SBP's terms, direct settlement, direct non-settlement, payment initiation service providers and indirect participants). This supports open banking, because fintechs that are not banks can now initiate payments on Raast directly rather than routing through a banking partner.
sourceTitle: PSP&OD Circular No. 01 of 2025: Raast Participation Criteria
label: Primary

headline: SBP Regulatory Sandbox Launched
annotation: SBP issued Guidelines for its own Regulatory Sandbox, separate from SECP's, in line with its Vision 2028. Testing runs in cohorts built around themes. The first cohort's themes, open banking, inward remittances and remote merchant onboarding, came with the shortlist in January 2026. If you are building an open banking product, this is likely the lowest risk path to regulatory approval.
sourceTitle: SBP issues the Guidelines for the Regulatory Sandbox (press release)
label: Primary

headline: Consolidated Customer Onboarding Framework
annotation: SBP issued the Consolidated Customer Onboarding Framework by circular on 25 July 2025, with compliance due within three months. It brings customer onboarding rules into one framework in which biometric verification through NADRA is the primary method, with NADRA Verisys as a fallback only where biometrics are not possible. For builders, account opening and wallet activation flows need NADRA biometric checks.
sourceTitle: BPRD Circular No. 01 of 2025: Consolidated Customer Onboarding Framework
label: Primary

headline: Digital Rupee CBDC Pilot Planned; Soramitsu Reported as Partner
annotation: SBP's governor said the bank was preparing a CBDC pilot, and Dawn, citing Nikkei Asia, reported that Japan's Soramitsu would work with SBP on it. In January 2026 the pilot was still described as planned, and SBP's FY26 payment systems review does not mention it. I found no official SBP notice that the pilot has started. For builders, a CBDC would be a new rail alongside Raast if it goes ahead.
sourceTitle: Pakistan picks Japanese company for digital currency rollout
label: Secondary

headline: PRISM+ Goes Live on ISO 20022
annotation: SBP launched PRISM+, the upgraded large value settlement system, moving the RTGS to the ISO 20022 messaging standard across retail and large value payments. For builders, ISO 20022 brings richer, structured payment data that reconciliation and compliance tools can use.
sourceTitle: Annual Payment Systems Review FY 2025-26
label: Primary

headline: 1LINK Designated as a Payment System
annotation: SBP notified 1LINK, which runs shared ATM switching, interbank transfers, bill payments and PayPak, as a Designated Payment System under the Payment Systems and Electronic Fund Transfers Act 2007. This brings closer oversight and alignment with international standards for infrastructure that many fintech flows depend on.
sourceTitle: Annual Payment Systems Review FY 2025-26
label: Primary

headline: Technology Risk Management Framework for Payment Institutions
annotation: PSP&OD Circular No. 04 of 2025 set baseline technology and cyber risk requirements for PSOs, PSPs and EMIs, covering security, fraud controls, third party and cloud risk, continuity and incident reporting, with compliance due by 31 March 2026. Any payment fintech needs these controls in place.
sourceTitle: PSP&OD Circular No. 04 of 2025: Technology Risk Management Framework for Payment Institutions
label: Primary

headline: NADRA Digital Identity and NDEL Regulations Announced
annotation: NADRA announced the Digital Identity Regulations 2025, which would let citizens verify identity online without physical documents, and the National Data Exchange Layer (NDEL) Regulations 2025, a framework for data sharing between government agencies and authorised private organisations. The press reported that the Ministry of Law and Justice had approved them. I could not find the official text or a date of effect. For fintechs, this points toward digital ID checks and structured data exchange in onboarding.
sourceTitle: NADRA issues landmark digital ID and data exchange regulations
label: Secondary

headline: PTA Critical Telecom Data and Infrastructure Security Regulations 2025 (draft)
annotation: PTA published draft Critical Telecom Data and Infrastructure Security Regulations 2025 for comment. As reported, they cover data localisation, a Chief Information Security Officer, yearly risk assessments and third party audits, and reporting of serious incidents within 24 hours, on a Zero Trust model. The press reported comments were open until 7 November 2025. Fintechs that rely on telecom channels for mobile money or USSD should watch how these rules affect their carriers.
sourceTitle: Critical Telecom Data and Infrastructure Security Regulations 2025
label: Primary

extraSources.title: PTA to enforce data localization and stricter cybersecurity for telcos
extraSources.label: Secondary

headline: First Regulatory Sandbox Cohort Shortlisted
annotation: Six applicants were shortlisted: three for open banking (Neem, Digi Khata, Swich Retail), one for remote merchant onboarding (The Bank of Punjab), and two for inward remittances (Barq Fintech, and Taptap Send UK with United Bank Limited). Testing runs for up to six months. Builders in adjacent spaces should study these participants, because they show where SBP wants evidence before writing rules.
sourceTitle: SBP announces the shortlisted applicants for the first cohort of its Regulatory Sandbox (press release)
label: Primary

headline: Raqami Islamic Digital Bank Becomes a Scheduled Bank
annotation: Raqami Islamic Digital Bank obtained scheduled bank status, after Mashreq Bank Pakistan in September 2025. Two more digital banks are now operating, which raises competition for digital first retail products.
sourceTitle: Annual Payment Systems Review FY 2025-26
label: Primary

headline: Cyber Shield Cyber Resilience Strategy (2025 to 2030)
annotation: CRMD Circular Letter No. 01 of 2026 launched a phased cyber resilience roadmap for SBP regulated entities, covering governance, detection and response, recovery, skills and third party risk. Regulated entities must align their own cybersecurity programmes with it.
sourceTitle: CRMD Circular Letter No. 01 of 2026: Launch of Cyber Shield Cyber Resilience Strategy for SBP Regulated Entities (2025 to 2030)
label: Primary

headline: Virtual Assets Act 2026 Enacted
annotation: The Virtual Assets Act 2026 received presidential assent on 4 March 2026 and came into force when it was published in the Gazette on 5 March 2026. It puts the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA), first set up under a 2025 ordinance, on a statutory footing, with powers to license and supervise virtual asset service providers. The press reported a focus on market surveillance and anti money laundering, with coordination with SBP and SECP.
sourceTitle: Virtual Assets Act, 2026 (Act No. XIII of 2026)
label: Primary

extraSources.title: Pakistan passes Virtual Assets Act 2026, empowers regulator to combat money laundering
extraSources.label: Secondary

headline: Banks Allowed to Serve Licensed Virtual Asset Service Providers
annotation: BPRD Circular Letter No. 10 of 2026 replaced SBP's 2018 circular on virtual currencies. Banks may open accounts for PVARA licensed providers, with client money kept in segregated, rupee denominated, non remunerative accounts and no cash deposits or withdrawals. This opens banking rails for licensed crypto businesses under tight controls.
sourceTitle: BPRD Circular Letter No. 10 of 2026: Authorizing Opening of Bank Accounts to PVARA's NOC/Licensed VASPs and their Customers
label: Primary

headline: Draft Open Banking Regulations 2026 Released for Consultation
annotation: SBP published draft Open Banking Regulations for public consultation. The draft would require banks, microfinance banks and EMIs to open APIs to licensed third party providers, with Raast as a central API hub and explicit, time bound, revocable customer consent. It is a draft, not yet in force. It follows the open banking sandbox cohort. For builders, this is the clearest signal yet of how account information and payment initiation services may work.
sourcePublisher: State Bank of Pakistan, Payment Systems Policy and Oversight Department
sourceTitle: Open Banking Regulations (Draft), for public consultation
label: Primary

extraSources.title: SBP releases draft Open Banking Regulations for public consultation
